    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly causally linked, with onboarding completion the upstream lever: accounts that never finish onboarding cannot activate. Two independent inherited records (memory_31, day 12; memory_86, day 52) point the same way and report durable rather than one-quarter lifts, which matters given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I verify memory_86 because it is the most recent and most directly on-point support for the action I intend, and memory_91 because activation messaging is the strongest competing use of the single slot and targets the larger decline directly — verifying both branches buys more decision-relevant information than double-confirming one side. Explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records exactly this move producing headline gains (+31% trials, +18% quarterly revenue) alongside a 12-point churn rise at renewal, and it carries a standing do-not-repeat-at-scale note. The competitive pressure is precisely the condition that makes that trap tempting; matching on price would buy revenue that the record says does not survive renewal. referral_incentive (memory_57) is credible but was established in existing customers and does not address either declining metric. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound for pipeline quality but is a different segment from the SMB accounts under attack. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: cutting required signup fields and onboarding steps can degrade the qualification data and demo-request path that memory_44 says drives enterprise pipeline quality, so the test should be scoped to SMB self-serve, leave the enterprise demo-request flow untouched, and instrument renewal-cohort retention rather than stopping at first-week activation. Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, the two onboarding records predate the current competitive environment, and I have not confirmed that the completion drop causes the activation drop rather than both sharing a third cause such as a shift in inbound traffic mix from the competitor. Verification may reverse this: if memory_86's source shows the lift was measured only on early engagement without renewal follow-through, or if memory_91 shows a larger and better-durability effect, I will switch to activation_messaging.
